To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

women with psychiatric disorders are at increased risk for substance use disorders and that women with alcohol and drug use disorders are at increased likelihood of developing clinically significant psychiatric disorders.
Women with co-occurrent substance use and psychiatric disorders have more severe substance use problems than women with substance use disorders alone.

(1) there is clinically significant comorbidity between substance use and psychiatric disorders, particularly in female substance abusers; (2) there is some evidence that women with co-morbid psychiatric and substance use conditions may respond better to gender-specific services than to traditional programs; and (3) women with substance use problems and psychiatric disorders are difficult to engage and retain, but physicians can play an important role in identifying and referring them to treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of anxiety disorders in substance abuse and the treatment of women with co-occuring psychiatric disorders.
the development and evaluation of interventions to prevent and treat substance use disorders in women and to improve the health and well-being of women who have experienced substance use disorders.
identifying and understanding the etiology, course, treatment, and prevention of psychiatric and substance abuse/dependence comorbidity in women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is insufficient to determine the effect on the outcomes of care of women with co-occuring psychiatric disorders and addictions.
there is a high degree of comorbidity between affective, anxiety, and substance use disorders in women.
there is a need for further research to determine effective treatment strategies for women with co-occuring disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women who have psychiatric disorders are at high risk for developing substance abuse/dependence, and women with substance abuse/dependence are at high risk of developing a psychiatric disorder.

women with psychiatric disorders are more likely than men to have substance use disorders, women with substance use disorders are more likely have psychiatric disorders, and women are less likely to receive adequate treatment for both.

the comorbidity between substance use and psychiatric disorders in women is high and clinically important.
there is a high degree of comorbidity between substance abuse and affective or anxiety disorder.
